biography.plain_text: James Arthur Ryder was an American transport entrepreneur who founded Ryder's truck-leasing business after starting with a single truck in Miami. Born in Columbus, Ohio, he moved to Florida as a child and worked in construction. After leaving the company bearing his name, he established the competing truck-rental business Jartran.

long_biography.plain_text:
Transport entrepreneur James Ryder wore two wristwatches to emphasise his promise of punctual deliveries. His company developed maintenance facilities at customers' premises and a wider service network, helping leased trucks operate beyond Florida. It also provided vehicles and drivers for the Miami Herald's daily distribution, combining equipment with an ongoing transport service.

Ryder helped establish Goodwill Industries of South Florida alongside Roy Perry and Leonard Abess. The organisation created employment and training opportunities for people facing barriers to work. The institution subsequently developed donated-goods retailing, service contracts and manufacturing work for people with disabilities.
